title: "Teaching"

::: {.justified}

I have taught for almost 20 years, in two countries, across business, ethics, and the social sciences, to students ranging from first-generation high schoolers to master's candidates.
Throughout these experiences the objective has not changed: to form men and women for others.
My courses rest on three pillars — skill development, practical application, and ethical reflection — and an ordinary class session covers all three.
I want my students to leave my classroom not only capable of performing technically difficult work, but also with a sense of what that capability is for and whom it is answerable to.

:::

::: {.justified}

## Ethics in Action

*Collegiate Scholars Program, University of Chicago — Instructor of Record, Summer 2026*

A course in applied ethics designed from scratch for high-achieving high school students on the threshold of university, most of them the first in their families to get there.
It moves deliberately across cases in business, technology, society, and government, so that ethical reasoning cannot be filed under a single domain and left there.
It is taught at the rigor of a College core course rather than as a preview of one.

[Syllabus](files/ethics-in-action-syllabus.pdf)

## Social Science Inquiry II

*The College, University of Chicago — Graduate Student Lecturer, 2024–25*

Statistics and research design, the methods course in the College's social sciences core sequence.
Students spend the first six weeks on structured R problem sets and the last three on a self-directed project, so that by the time they choose a question the tools are no longer the obstacle.
Sessions alternate between lecture, guided discussion, and hands-on workshop, and every technique is anchored to a policy or organizational question someone would actually want answered.

[Syllabus](files/ssi-syllabus.pdf) · [Student evaluations](files/ssi-2025-evaluations.pdf)

## Professional Ethics · Fundamentals of Ethics

*VALIA, Monterrey — Professor, 2016–2023*

A certificate program in business ethics serving roughly four hundred students drawn from five universities in Monterrey.
Most students work, which is where the course gets tested: the cases they bring from their own jobs are harder than the ones in the casebook.
I kept teaching here through the pandemic and through a doctorate in another country.

[Evaluation reports](files/valia-evaluations.pdf)

## Corporate Finance

*Universidad de Monterrey — Associate Professor, 2014–2015*

Students evaluated real investment pitches I had received as an investor, and I told them which ones I funded and why.
I redesigned the course to build ethics cases and a finance simulator into the regular coursework.

## International Accounting

*Tec de Monterrey (ITESM) — Associate Professor, 2013–2016*

The last of eight accounting courses and taken only by accounting majors.
I redesigned it to integrate ethics cases, and students learned accrual basis by reading actual invoices and bank statements rather than textbook exhibits.

[Institutional ranking, Fall 2013](files/itesm-2013-ranking.pdf)

## Introduction to Computing · English as a Second Language · Social Science Research Methods

*PrepaNet, Tec de Monterrey (ITESM), Tampico — Instructor, 2008–2012*

PrepaNet is Tec de Monterrey's social program, founded in 2004, offering a complete high school education to young people and adults for whom finishing one had otherwise been out of reach.
I taught three courses in Tampico to students earning their degree alongside work and family obligations, first in person and later online as the program moved to a fully remote format.
It is the teaching that most shaped how I think about access: what stood between those students and a diploma was never ability.

:::
